steps.question: Do the 5 paired control/treated blood samples per subject cluster by subject and by condition, and is any of the 10 samples an outlier or mislabeled, before fitting the paired model?

grounding.reason: Raw-count dataset: mandatory blind-VST/PCA/distance-heatmap QC before any paired model is fit (M-0006, tpl-qc-eda).

steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes have enough counts across the paired control/treated blood samples to be tested?

grounding.reason: Minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=5 samples, the smallest group size); independent filtering in the results step does the rest.

acceptance_criteria: Keep a gene only if it has at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples (the smallest group size)
Report the number of genes retained vs the 12000 starting genes

steps.name: Paired DESeq2 model and Wald test (subject + condition)
steps.question: Which genes respond to treatment within each of the 5 subjects, controlling for between-subject variation, in the design ~subject + condition with control as the reference level?

grounding.reason: Paired design blocks on subject (~subject+condition, R-0011); STAR/featureCounts raw counts go straight into DESeq2 with no length correction (R-0064); explicit control reference level (R-0036, checked with knowledge_check — 'control' is a valid explicit choice per R-0036, warning noted and accepted since the dataset names an actual control condition); apeglm-shrunk LFC reported beside unshrunken (R-0009/R-0085); BH FDR at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering (R-0010/R-0043); edgeR QL run as the second method for a robustness/intersection check (R-0042/R-0001).

acceptance_criteria: DESeqDataSet built from the raw integer count matrix and the metadata (subject, condition) with design = ~subject + condition
condition factor releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference level
DESeq() run with default median-of-ratios size factors and the Wald test on the condition coefficient
results() extracted with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering on
apeglm log2FoldChange shrinkage applied to the condition coefficient and reported alongside the unshrunken LFC and its SE
MA plot and dispersion plot produced as fit diagnostics
Count outliers flagged via Cook's distance reported separately from independent-filtering NAs
p-value histogram inspected and reported before trusting BH-adjusted values

edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test run on the same filtered counts and design (~subject+condition) as a robustness check; DESeq2 vs edgeR significant-gene overlap reported, intersection treated as the high-confidence set

steps.name: GSEA preranked enrichment: Hallmark and Reactome
steps.context: Reference gene sets: the MSigDB human Hallmark GMT and the Reactome human pathway GMT (member gene symbols, HGNC) staged in this environment's pathway reference collection. If a resource is unexpectedly absent at run time, fall back to the WikiPathways human GMT also staged here and state the substitution.
steps.question: Which Hallmark and Reactome pathways are enriched among genes ranked by their within-subject treatment response (DESeq2 Wald statistic)?

grounding.reason: Ranked GSEA on full gene list with Wald statistic as the chosen ranking metric (disputed rule R-0007, side chosen: Wald stat, per R-0099); Hallmark first then Reactome for human (R-0048/R-0098), both confirmed present as MSigDB 2026.1 Hallmark and Reactome-current GMTs in this environment; size window 15-500 (R-0047); ORA on a short significant list is underpowered (R-0103) so GO ORA, if run, uses the tested-gene universe.

acceptance_criteria: Full tested gene list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column), no pre-filtering by significance
fgsea run against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets and separately against the Reactome human gene sets, each restricted to sets with 15-500 member genes intersecting the tested genes
BH-adjusted enrichment p-values reported per collection
Leading-edge genes reported for every significant gene set, with redundant/overlapping significant sets collapsed to representatives

If fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05 in T1S3, state this explicitly and do not additionally run an ORA on that short list — GO BP ORA (if attempted) uses the full tested-gene universe from T1S2/T1S3, not just the significant subset
Gene set database name and version stated for each collection used

steps.name: Differential expression and enrichment report
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible summary of within-subject treatment-responsive genes and their enriched pathways in this paired 5-subject blood dataset?

grounding.reason: Report step assembles the mandated reproducibility record, fit diagnostics, dual-effect-size gene table, and enrichment provenance per the report-step rule set.

acceptance_criteria: Report states the design formula (~subject+condition), the reference level, the contrast (condition treated vs control), the FDR cutoff (padj<0.05), and the number of genes tested after filtering
Gene table includes shrunken and unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, p-value, padj for every tested gene; ranked by shrunken LFC for display
MA plot and dispersion plot included as fit diagnostics
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap of significant genes reported as the high-confidence set
Enrichment section states the gene set database and version, ranking metric, universe, and size window used, with leading-edge genes per significant set
Full reproducibility record included: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seeds, gene-set collection versions

plan.title: Paired DESeq2 treatment-vs-control DE in blood
plan.analytical_narrative: Five subjects each contribute a control and a treated blood sample, so the within-subject treatment effect is estimated by blocking on subject in a paired DESeq2 design (~subject + condition). We first inspect sample structure (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm the 10 samples pair correctly and no sample is an outlier before fitting the model. After a minimal count pre-filter, DESeq2 fits the Wald test on the design ~subject + condition with control as the explicit reference level, reports apeglm-shrunken log2 fold changes, and applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05 to call treatment-responsive genes within subjects. As a robustness check, edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is run on the same design/counts and the DESeq2/edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence set. The resulting Wald-statistic-ranked full gene list feeds fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets (with GO BP over-representation as a named-list follow-up, contingent on having enough significant genes), giving pathway-level context for what changed with treatment. A final report step assembles fit diagnostics, the gene table (shrunken and unshrunken LFC), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and the full reproducibility record.

DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, session info, reproducibility record
